name: Deliverance
momentumNotes: Tension loosens; once release appears, simplicity and forgiveness help the movement complete.
theme: Deliverance is the storm breaking and the knot loosening. Energy that was trapped can return to movement.
basicInterpretation: Let what has been tense begin to release. Act promptly where release is possible, and do not keep carrying what has already opened.

reversed.theme: Flipped upside down, Deliverance becomes Hexagram 39, Obstruction. This other side brings in the atmosphere of difficulty, delay, help, asking how the situation may look from another threshold.
reversed.reflection: Let Obstruction widen the reading rather than replace it. Consider what another person, timing, or hidden part of you might see when the pattern is viewed from the far side.
reversed.applicationPrompt: Visualize your question from the far side, as if another person or your future self is looking back through Obstruction. Notice where difficulty, delay, help and a blocked, turning movement reveal needs, timing, or motives that the first view may miss.

opposite.theme: The contrast to Deliverance is Hexagram 37, The Family. Where the primary pattern emphasizes release, relief, untangling, this complementary field points toward home, roles, care.
opposite.reflection: This is not the main movement of the reading, but it shows what balances or challenges it. It can also highlight hidden causes or contrasting forces at play. Notice where The Family names the medicine, shadow, or unchosen path beside the situation.
opposite.applicationPrompt: Visualize The Family as the contrasting color laid beside Deliverance. Ask what hidden cause, missing medicine, or opposing pressure is suggested by home, roles, care, especially where the situation carries a supportive, disciplined tone.
